args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service started failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. Rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and check why it was promoted to production when the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again. The SEV2 incident is open as **INC-0001**.

1. **Rollback:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
2. **Check after rollback:** All three regions are on v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
3. **Incident:** I opened INC-0001, "checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0", which pages the on-call engineer. The request timed out, so I didn't resend it. When I checked the incident list, it showed exactly one incident, so there's no duplicate page. The incident summary describes the failure and the rollback, and lists next steps.

The v2.3.1 release candidate was also failing in staging but still went to production. The incident's next steps include finding out why it was promoted anyway and finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure.
